div.head: IX Atr Prol.
div.ab: (Incip.) [Wanley] Ðis is seo gerædnes þe Æþelred cyning and ealle his witan æt Wudestoce geræddan.
Ðis is sio gerædnes þe Æþelred cyning and ealle his witan æt Wudustoce geræddan.
This is the ordinance which King Æthelred and all his councillors have determined upon at Woodstock.
This is the decree which King Æthelred and his whole council proclaimed at Woodstock.
IX Atr. Prol. Dies ist die Verordnung, die König Aethelred und alle seine Witan zu Woodstock beschlossen haben.
IX Atr. Prologue. This is the ordinance which King Æthelred and all his witan decided at Woodstock.
div.note: Only source: Cotton Otho A X (now burnt), known from Wanley's extract in Hickes, Thesaurus III 232 (Wanley writes wynn as þ). Dated c. 980–1016. Liebermann compares I Atr Prol.

Manuscripts: MS = London, British Library, Cotton MS Otho A.x. Since the manuscript was almost completely destroyed in the Ashburnam House fire of 1731, this edition relies on the text of Liebermann, Gesetze, vol. 1, p. 269. Exp And: An MS healdan: healed MS holdliche: Liebermann recommends emending to holdlice, though holdliche is a legitimate late form of the word
Due to damage to the manuscript, this text is based on that found in Lie bermann, Die Gesetze der Angelsachsen.

Woodstock: Woodstock, Oxfordshire, had been the site of an earlier meeting of the royal council in approximately 997, at which the legislation 1 Æthelred was issued. The meeting at which this text was compiled likely took place between 1008 and 1016.
